frontMatter.value: Test-first development at any step: discover the repository's own test commands, name the break a test catches, watch it fail for the intended reason, make it pass with the smallest change, and add a new test only where it catches a realistic failure the existing ones would miss. Use when writing or changing a test, building a feature or fixing a bug test-first, or deciding whether a change needs a new test; also on 'red-green-refactor' and integration tests.

passages.text: tdd is the habit for the moment a test is written or changed, a change's need for a new test is weighed, or code is built or a bug fixed test-first, at whatever step the work is in, most often build. It writes no record of its own: the tests and the checks it leaves belong to the step that runs, and that step's section names them. Whether a change gains a new test is judged on its cost, below; a behavior change with no check that could fail is a floor in AGENTS.md, so leave one wherever you can: an existing test that fails if the change breaks, a new test, or the closest executable check. The shape of a seam is deep-modules', a bug whose cause is not yet known is diagnose's first, and removing a test is sweep-tests', with its mutation proof: this habit never deletes a test.

## When a new test earns its place

Before adding a test, name the realistic failure it would catch and why the tests already there, or a simpler check, would miss it; with no answer, add none. Extend an existing test before writing a new one, and cover the behavior with the smallest set of cases that does. A test is never added to raise a coverage figure or a test count, or to make the work look finished. Zero new tests is a valid outcome only where an existing test already fails if this change breaks, so the change still leaves a check that could fail. Copy, styling, documentation, configuration and plain wiring are normally checked by inspection, the type checker, the build or a direct run, unless a concrete risk calls for a test.
